research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Historic England, GOV.UK and Planning Data heritage sources checked on 25 July 2026. Designation points, indicative outlines, conservation-area work-in-progress data, NHLE records, consent guidance and Heritage at Risk information are not parcel-title boundaries, planning outcomes, consent decisions or Future Growth scores.

verification.method: Direct official web verification; point/outline/curtilage, designation/consent, current-register/work-in-progress distinctions enforced.

source_facts.fact: Historic England states the NHLE is the only official up-to-date register of nationally protected historic buildings and sites; listed-building GIS data was updated 14 July 2026 and scheduled monuments/parks/battlefields/world heritage downloads 23 July 2026.
source_facts.gate: Downloaded geometry must retain its dataset date and cannot substitute for title or parcel boundaries.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data reports 382,254 listed-building records and states the point does not define the extent affected by listing.
source_facts.gate: Listed-building point proximity is not an extent or curtilage determination.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data reports 124,897 outlines and explicitly says coverage is incomplete and curtilage is not consistently shown.
source_facts.gate: Outline intersection is indicative and needs further checks before planning decisions.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data reports 11,007 conservation areas from 158 providers and warns the dataset is incomplete and contains duplicates.
source_facts.gate: Missing or duplicated service data must not be converted into definitive designation status.

source_facts.fact: Works affecting the character of a listed building generally require Listed Building Consent; unauthorised relevant works can be a criminal offence.
source_facts.gate: Listing does not mean all change is prohibited and consent need is work-specific.

source_facts.fact: Written Scheduled Monument Consent is required before most works to a scheduled monument; planning permission may also be separately required.
source_facts.gate: SMC and planning permission are separate regimes and neither may be inferred from designation alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Listed Building Consent semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Consent is required for demolition, alteration or extension affecting special character; listing does not freeze all change.

official_measurement_examples.name: Scheduled Monument Consent semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Most works require written SMC; planning permission may separately be required.

core_rules: NHLE designation is not a planning permission outcome
listed building point is not the affected-area boundary
listed building point proximity is not curtilage evidence
listed building outline is indicative where coverage is incomplete
listed building outline must not be treated as title boundary
curtilage requires legal and factual assessment beyond a service polygon
listing protects significance but does not prohibit all change
Listed Building Consent need depends on proposed works and effect on character
planning permission and Listed Building Consent are separate decisions
absence of planning permission does not imply absence of LBC need
existence of planning permission does not imply LBC has been granted
unauthorised relevant listed-building works must not be represented as regularised
scheduled monument designation is not Scheduled Monument Consent
SMC and planning permission must remain separate
Class Consent exceptions must not be generalized to every scheduled-monument work
scheduled-monument geometry must be date-versioned
Historic England download date is not designation date
NHLE list entry text and GIS representation serve different evidential purposes
Planning Data heritage records must retain origin-quality warnings
Planning Data scheduled-monument geometry must be checked against current NHLE where material
conservation-area service data is incomplete and duplicates can exist
missing conservation-area record does not prove a site is outside a conservation area
duplicate conservation-area records must not be double-counted
conservation-area designation is not automatic refusal of development
Article 4 controls must not be assumed merely from conservation-area membership
tree controls in conservation areas require their own procedural checks
world heritage status does not by itself create a standalone UK consent regime
World Heritage Site planning protection must not be reduced to a binary parcel score
registered heritage significance is not a market-value estimate
Heritage at Risk status is not planning refusal or structural-survey evidence
absence from Heritage at Risk does not prove good physical condition
Heritage at Risk register year must be preserved
heritage-setting effects can extend beyond a designation polygon
mere distance from a heritage asset is not a setting-impact conclusion
historic environment significance requires asset-specific evidence
non-designated heritage assets must not be assumed absent because NHLE has no entry
local-list status must remain distinct from national designation
certificate of immunity status must not be inferred from absence of listing
building preservation notice is not permanent listing unless later designated
de-designated records must not be treated as current designations
planning consultation with Historic England is not consent
Historic England advice is not the local planning authority decision
energy retrofit guidance for historic buildings does not grant consent
climate adaptation does not override heritage consent requirements
policy guidance is not a parcel-specific heritage statement
service counts are metadata not parcel evidence
NO_DATA must not be interpreted as no heritage constraint
no parcel relation, consent result or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
